newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss turn down Mobutu's visa request.
newsitem.headline: Swiss turn down Mobutu's visa request.

text.p: Switzerland has turned down a visa request from Zaire's ailing ruler Mobutu Sese Seko, who is currently in France and wants to return to the country for medical treatment, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.
Spokesman Hans Ruedi Bortis told Reuters: "There was a new request (from Mobutu) for a visa. This request will not be accepted. A visa will not be granted."

Mobutu, 66, underwent more than two months of treatment for prostate cancer in Lausanne. The Zairean ruler, who said last week that he intended to return to Lausanne for a medical check-up, left Switzerland on November 4 for the French Riviera where he has a villa.
Bortis said Mobutu's departure meant the medical grounds for a possible extension of his Swiss visa did not exist anymore.

"From the point of view of the Swiss foreign ministry, with the departure of Mr Mobutu, the medical reason for a new visa does not exist anymore. We do not have to explain further why we do not issue a new visa," he said.

Swiss official sources said Mobutu applied for a new visa to return to Switzerland on Friday. Mobutu's absence from Zaire has raised fears that the vast central African country may disintegrate following a successful Tutsi revolt in the east.
